subject: lauder

brief.inclusion: Estée Lauder heir, former Reagan appointee and president of the World Jewish Congress since 2007, who has given about $21.6 million in itemized federal contributions, mostly to Republican super PACs, spent millions more in New York state politics, served as a private channel between Israeli and Arab leaders and Donald Trump, and in 2026 stopped his political giving and broke publicly with Benjamin Netanyahu.
brief.namesakes: FEC rows for Ronald Lauderbach (San Diego), Ronald A. Lauderdale (Greenwich) and "Lauder, Ronald Mrs." (his wife, Jo Carole Lauder) are excluded. The subject files from New York or Washington with Estée Lauder, Clinique, RSL Management, U.S. government or investor employers.

coverage.lags: FEC Schedule A shows no gift after December 2025 in the matched rows; a January 2026 $5,000 gift reported by the New York Times may file under a variant name. New York State Board of Elections giving (Safe Together NY, Save Our State NY, term-limits campaigns) is outside the federal record.

openQuestions: 1989 mayoral spending: reported as about $13–14 million in later accounts; the Christian Science Monitor gave $8.5 million a month before the primary. Confirm the final figure from Campaign Finance Board records.
Pentagon appointment year: Forbes says 1983–1986; Wikipedia's body says 1984.
2022 New York governor race: New York Focus counts $9.05 million to two pro-Zeldin PACs; the New York Times reported more than $11 million. Reconcile from state filings.
Syria track (1998): Lauder says Netanyahu agreed to a Golan withdrawal; Netanyahu has denied it. Lauder says he holds the two copies of the draft.
Son-in-law Kevin Warsh's current Federal Reserve role needs a primary source before it is recorded.

summary: Son of Estée Lauder and heir to the cosmetics company, he served Ronald Reagan as a Pentagon official and ambassador to Austria, ran for mayor of New York in 1989, and has been president of the World Jewish Congress since 2007. He has given about $21.6 million in itemized federal contributions, mostly to Republican super PACs, including $5 million to the pro-Trump MAGA Inc. in March 2025, and was the leading funder of Lee Zeldin's 2022 run for governor. In 2026 he stopped political giving and, days before Israel's election, called his former friend Benjamin Netanyahu "a dictator."

chapters.title: The younger son of Estée Lauder
chapters.dek: A cosmetics fortune, a Wharton degree and a lifetime at the family company.
chapters.body:
Lauder was born in New York City on February 26, 1944, the younger son of Estée and Joseph Lauder, founders of the cosmetics company [[wikipedia]]. He went to the Bronx High School of Science and graduated from the Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania in 1965, after joining the family company in 1964 [[wikipedia, dp-epstein-2026]].

The company is the source of his wealth. He sat on its board for nearly fifty years, apart from 2009 to 2016, has chaired Clinique Laboratories since 1994 and retired from the board in 2025 [[forbes-profile]]. Forbes puts his net worth at $5.4 billion; Estée Lauder's shares fell by roughly three-quarters from their 2021 peak, and by mid-2025 he had pledged nearly all his Class B shares as loan collateral [[forbes-profile, fortune-2026]].

He is also one of the world's major collectors of Austrian and German modernist art. He opened the Neue Galerie in New York in 2001 and in 2006 paid $135 million, then a record, for Gustav Klimt's Portrait of Adele Bloch-Bauer I [[wikipedia]].

chapters.title: The Pentagon and Vienna
chapters.dek: A Republican donor's appointments under Reagan.
chapters.body:
Lauder gave to Republican candidates from the late 1970s, and Ronald Reagan brought him into government [[fec-lauder]]. He served as deputy assistant secretary of defense for European and NATO policy in the mid-1980s and, in 1985, published Fighting Violent Crime in America [[forbes-profile, wikipedia]].

Reagan then named him ambassador to Austria. He was appointed on April 16, 1986, presented his credentials that May and left the post in October 1987 [[state-austria]]. The experience turned his philanthropy toward Jewish Europe: in 1987 he established the Ronald S. Lauder Foundation to rebuild Jewish life in Central and Eastern Europe [[wikipedia]].

chapters.title: Running for mayor, and against City Hall
chapters.dek: A self-funded primary campaign against Rudy Giuliani and two term-limits referendums.
chapters.body:
In 1989 Lauder ran for mayor of New York as a Republican, financing the campaign himself and declining the city's new public-financing system. "I don't want to use taxpayers' money," he said; by August he had spent $8.5 million [[csm-1989]]. He pitched himself as a manager, saying the city was "a $26.6 billion business, and should be run that way" [[csm-1989]]. He lost the September primary to Rudy Giuliani with 33 percent of the vote; later accounts put his total spending at about $13 million or more [[wikipedia]].

He stayed in city politics through the ballot. He led and funded the 1993 referendum that imposed term limits on New York's elected officials, and the 1996 campaign that defeated the City Council's attempt to extend them, spending about $4 million across the two [[wikipedia]].

chapters.title: Netanyahu's envoy
chapters.dek: A secret Syria track, a television station and a friendship that broke.
chapters.body:
Lauder was close to Benjamin Netanyahu from the 1980s and introduced him to the American political consultant Arthur Finkelstein, who had worked on Lauder's own campaign [[wikipedia]]. During Netanyahu's first term he became the prime minister's secret envoy to Hafez al-Assad. By Lauder's account in 2026, he spent ten to fifteen months in 1998 traveling between Israel, Syria and Lebanon and helped draft a ten-point framework that Netanyahu accepted, including withdrawal from the Golan Heights, before backing out; he says he holds the only two copies of the final draft [[toi-2026]]. Netanyahu has denied agreeing to give up the Golan [[toi-2026, wikipedia]].

The friendship broke over Israeli television. Lauder became the controlling shareholder of Channel 10, which Netanyahu had urged him to buy and which then reported critically on him. In 2011 the channel was accused of airing an apology to Sheldon Adelson under shareholder pressure; Israel's broadcast regulator found no interference [[wikipedia]]. The channel, Lauder said in 2026, "destroyed" the relationship [[toi-2026]].

chapters.title: President of the World Jewish Congress
chapters.dek: Two decades as the international face of organized Jewish communities.
chapters.body:
In June 2007 Lauder was elected president of the World Jewish Congress, succeeding Edgar Bronfman Sr. [[wikipedia]]. He has used the post to press European governments and companies on Iran, Holocaust memory and antisemitism, from Swiss gas deals with Tehran to Polish Holocaust legislation, and in 2025 said the 1998 Swiss banks settlement should be reopened [[wikipedia]].

After the October 7, 2023, attacks he turned that pressure on his own university. He wrote to Penn's president, Liz Magill, that a campus Palestinian literature festival had "put a deep stain on Penn's reputation" and that he was reexamining his support[[cnn-penn-2023]].

chapters.title: A Republican megadonor in the Trump era
chapters.dek: Greenland, Zeldin and $5 million to MAGA Inc.
chapters.body:
Lauder has known Donald Trump since college, and by Peter Baker and Susan Glasser's account he was the "really, really experienced businessman" who first pitched Trump on buying Greenland, early in his first term; Denmark rejected the idea when it became public in 2019 [[baker-greenland-2022]]. Forbes describes him as an informal White House adviser on Israel [[forbes-profile]].

His federal giving rose sharply after 2016. FEC records show about $21.6 million in itemized contributions since 1978, more than three-quarters of it after 2017, led by $5.5 million to the Senate Leadership Fund, $5 million to MAGA Inc. and $4.65 million to National Horizon, a New York-focused Republican super PAC [[fec-lauder]]. The MAGA Inc. check, on March 24, 2025, came two months after Trump's second inauguration [[fec-lauder, fortune-2026]].

His largest single campaign was in New York state politics, outside the federal record. In 2022 he gave $9.05 million to two PACs supporting Lee Zeldin's challenge to Governor Kathy Hochul, among the largest individual gifts in state records, and $61,000 to Zeldin directly [[nyfocus-2022]].

chapters.title: Closing the wallet and breaking with Netanyahu
chapters.dek: Epstein files, a sudden stop to political giving and a public break before Israel's election.
chapters.body:
In February 2026 Justice Department releases of Jeffrey Epstein's records showed Lauder in contact with Epstein years after his 2008 conviction. Epstein had supervised the creation of Friends Ventures LLC, through which Lauder and Leon Black co-owned a $25 million Kurt Schwitters painting from 2014, and contacts continued into 2017. Lauder has not been accused of wrongdoing [[dp-epstein-2026]].

That August the New York Times reported that one of the Republican Party's most reliable donors had stopped giving. His last federal gift was $5,000 in January 2026, he had made no donations to New York Republicans that year, his super PAC had gone inactive and he had let go of advisers who had worked for him for decades. Associates said his children had pressed him to cut spending; a person close to the family said there was no financial difficulty [[nyt-wallet-2026, fortune-2026]].

On October 22, five days before Israel's Knesset election, he broke a long public silence about Netanyahu. In an interview with Haaretz he called the prime minister "a dictator — a one-person show," said that "if Bibi is elected, Israel stands to lose badly," and warned that Israel had lost the Democratic Party and was "losing the Republican Party." He said he would back Gadi Eisenkot if forced to choose, had sold or given away his Israeli properties and would not return, while remaining "still a Zionist" [[haaretz-2026, toi-2026]].
